verdict.rationale: Obsidian is a Markdown note editor, and hands-on reports describe a fast, keyboard-friendly experience: a Command Palette, a built-in vim mode, and an editor that is fast and gets out of the way. The pack never explicitly documents headings, callouts, tables, code blocks or embedded media, so most of the formatting elements are only implied by Markdown. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of callouts, tables, code blocks, headings and media embeds, plus keyboard shortcut and editor-performance documentation.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can write and format notes with headings, callouts, tables, code blocks, and embedded media in a fast keyboard-driven editor

citations.quote: Obsidian stores your notes as Markdown-formatted plain text files in a vault.
Built-in vim mode works surprisingly well, with minor cursor-blinking glitches.
fast and gets out of the way
